findings.evidence: Sobolev/Local/Basic.lean:142 defines `MemWkpLoc (p) (U : Set ℂ)` with `HasWeakFDerivOn volume (Opens.interior U)`, and line 160 `memWkpLoc_succ_iff_of_isOpen` is the open-set bridge. Weak.lean:217 `isWeakCauchyRiemannUpToBoundaryOn_coe_iff` shows the open predicate is the special case.
findings.fix: Keep one predicate, `IsWeakCauchyRiemannOn p (U : Set ℂ)`, with the current up-to-boundary body. Add one `isWeakCauchyRiemannOn_iff_of_isOpen` unfolding lemma (HasWeakFDerivOn on Ω and ae on Ω) and prove the elementary API once.
findings.issue: Two predicates are defined: `IsWeakCauchyRiemannOn` on `Opens ℂ` and `IsWeakCauchyRiemannUpToBoundaryOn` on `Set ℂ`, although the first is the second restricted to open sets (simp lemma `isWeakCauchyRiemannUpToBoundaryOn_coe_iff`). As a result, continuousOn, memLpLoc, memWkpLoc_one, completeSpace, ae_eq_of_hasWeakFDerivOn, mono, mono_exponent and _iff_forall_hasWeakFDerivOn are each proved twice.

findings.evidence: `abbrev IsWeakLinearCauchyRiemannOn (p) (Ω : Opens ℂ) ... := IsWeakCauchyRiemannOn p Ω ...`, and nothing in the diff gives an up-to-boundary counterpart.
findings.fix: After merging into a single set-based predicate, state `IsWeakLinearCauchyRiemannOn p (U : Set ℂ) A C ξ` and its closure lemmas for arbitrary `U`.
findings.issue: `IsWeakLinearCauchyRiemannOn` and its `add`, `const_smul` and `zero` are built only on the open-set predicate. The linear equation therefore has no version on half-discs, the case the up-to-boundary predicate is meant for; this is a result of the split definition.

summary: The open-set predicate is a special case of the up-to-boundary predicate (`isWeakCauchyRiemannUpToBoundaryOn_coe_iff` proves this), yet both are defined and every elementary lemma is proved twice, and the linear equation exists only for the open-set version. Library precedent (`MemWkpLoc`) uses one set-based predicate with `_of_isOpen` bridging lemmas.
